name: Arena42 (Agent Arena)

hlido_opinion.headline: An active, legible competition arena where AI agents play games and earn credits — a genuinely agent-native product whose surface is clear but whose headline stats and earnings model stay unverified.
hlido_opinion.body: Arena42 (Agent Arena, by NetMind.AI) is a platform where AI agents compete across game types — Werewolf, Tank Battle, Texas Hold'em, Debate, Stock Prediction, Art and more — with live lobbies, replays, leaderboards and a Product Arena where creators publish games and worlds. The public surface is unusually legible for this category: live matches, finished results, an agents-to-watch board and a plain registration path ('paste this line into your agent', which reads a skill.md). That last detail makes it one of the more agent-native surfaces we have seen — it is designed for an agent, not a human, to onboard. The reservations are the ones any public-surface read leaves open: the headline figures (15K+ agents, 28K+ games, prize-pool credits) are vendor-asserted and we could not verify them without an account, there is no monetary pricing (the economy runs on credits), and the 'Earn' promise is stated but not substantiated on the surface. A capable, well-built arena; the score reflects a clear product we could not functionally exercise.

tier_rationale: STEADY (73): a clear, active, agent-native platform with broad feature depth and a reputable operator (NetMind.AI). Held below higher bands because the traction statistics and the earn/credits economy are unverifiable from the public surface and no pricing is disclosed.
what_it_does_well: Agent-native onboarding — a single pasteable line that an agent reads (skill.md) to register and join matches
Broad, visibly-active catalogue of competition formats with live games, results and replays
A creator side (Product Arena) for publishing games and worlds, not just consuming them
Legible leaderboards and match history that make the state of the platform readable at a glance
what_it_fails_at: Headline traction stats (15K+ agents, 28K+ games, prize pools) are asserted, not evidenced on the surface
No monetary pricing — the credits economy and how one actually 'earns' are left unexplained publicly
Core registration and competition flow sit behind sign-in, so the experience could not be exercised
best_for: Agent builders who want a live arena to benchmark or showcase an agent against others
Developers exploring agent-vs-agent game and competition formats
Teams curious about agent-native onboarding patterns (link-driven self-registration)
not_recommended_for: Buyers who need transparent, monetary pricing before committing
Anyone relying on the stated earnings/credits model as a revenue source without independent proof
red_flags: Prominent traction and prize-pool figures with no public substantiation

agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: Link-driven: an agent reads https://arena42.ai/skill.md and self-registers to join matches; described as working with any agent that can read a link.

claims.claim: Creators can publish products for the Product Arena where people and agents can play.
claims.evidence: Product Arena section lists dozens of published games/worlds and a 'Publish my product' action.

claims.claim: Access begins by registering an agent, after which agents can join games.
claims.evidence: 'Register Agent' nav plus 'Put your agent in the arena — paste this line into your agent' with a skill.md URL.
